newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS TO CONTINUE LOW-COST JOB SHIFTS.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS TO CONTINUE LOW-COST JOB SHIFTS.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Wednesday it would continue to move jobs to cheap labour countries in its battle to cut costs.

Philips recently resolved a dispute over job cuts at its Hoogeveen plant in the eastern Netherlands under plans to relocate some of the plant's production to Poland as part of a wider strategy of wage-cost reductions.
"We have to remain competitive," Philips vice chairman Dudley Eustace said in response to a question at the company's first quarter 1997 results news conference.
He said said some 26 percent of Philips employees worked in low labour cost countries around the world, pointing out this still represented only seven percent of total wages.
"So as the headcount is quite a large number... the effect on the bottom line in terms of wage costs is still quite small," he said, adding the trend of moving jobs woud continue.

"We have identified Poland as a country where we continue to invest strongly and where further production of goods will move from Western countries to Eastern lands and that is all in the name of the pressure on costs," Eustace said.
He said the trend would be quite slow, but methodical.

"We have got around 260,000 employees around the world and you need to make huge inroads...tens of thousands of jobs will have to move to low cost countries in order to make much difference in that number and that won't happen in the short term," he told reporters.
"It tends to be a slow progress over the years and I don't see any great swing...by the end of this year," Eustace added.
"Across the board, profits are better. Essentially because we are continuing to attack costs and that will remain the case," said Eustace.
